description: Extensive question bank derived from Karnataka Government FDA/SDA examination notes (Section 7.6). Covers Governor, Chief Minister, Council of Ministers, Karnataka Legislature, Legislative Assembly, Legislative Council, Karnataka High Court, and State/district administration. Each question is mapped to a specific constitutional Article or administrative fact from the source document. Verify current office-holders from official notifications before formal examination use.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which system of government does Karnataka follow under the Constitution?

options.C: Federal system with unitary features only

questions.explanation: Karnataka follows the parliamentary system of government, as stated in the Karnataka Government notes.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who is the highest law officer of the State of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Advocate General is the State's highest law officer.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The State Legislature of Karnataka consists of which of the following?

options.B: Governor, Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council
options.C: Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council only

questions.explanation: Under Article 168, the Karnataka Legislature consists of the Governor, the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Section A and D

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Part of the Constitution deals with the State Executive?
questions.explanation: State Executive is covered under Part VI, Articles 153-167.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Articles 168 to 212 of the Constitution deal with which subject?
questions.explanation: State Legislature is covered under Part VI, Articles 168-212.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Articles of the Constitution deal with High Courts?
questions.explanation: High Courts are covered under Part VI, Articles 214-231.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Articles 233 to 237 of the Constitution deal with which subject?
questions.explanation: Subordinate courts are covered under Articles 233-237.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for the Advocate General of a State?
questions.explanation: Article 165 provides for the Advocate General of a State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: State Public Service Commission is covered under which Articles?
questions.explanation: State Public Service Commission is covered under Articles 315-323.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: State Election Commission is covered under which Articles?
questions.explanation: State Election Commission is covered under Articles 243K and 243ZA.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Is Karnataka a unicameral or bicameral State?
questions.explanation: Karnataka is bicameral because its Legislature has two Houses: the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for the creation or abolition of a Legislative Council?
questions.explanation: Article 169 deals with the creation or abolition of a Legislative Council.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides that there shall be a Governor for each State?
questions.explanation: Article 153 provides that there shall be a Governor for each State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Can the same person be appointed Governor for two or more States?
questions.explanation: Article 153 provides that the same person may be appointed Governor for two or more States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who appoints the Governor of Karnataka?

options.A: Chief Justice of the High Court

questions.explanation: The President of India appoints the Governor by warrant under his or her hand and seal under Article 155.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article does the Governor hold office during the pleasure of the President?
questions.explanation: Under Article 156, the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the normal term of office of a Governor?
questions.explanation: The normal term is five years from the date of entering office, under Article 156.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article specifies the qualifications to become Governor?
questions.explanation: Under Article 157, a person must be a citizen of India and must have completed 35 years of age.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the minimum age to become a Governor?
questions.explanation: Under Article 157, a person must have completed 35 years of age.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 158, which of the following conditions applies to the Governor?

options.A: The Governor must be a member of the Legislative Assembly
options.B: The Governor cannot be a member of Parliament or a State Legislature
options.C: The Governor must be a resident of the State
options.D: The Governor must be a retired judge

questions.explanation: Article 158 provides that the Governor cannot be a member of Parliament or a State Legislature.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: If a member of Parliament is appointed Governor, what happens to the seat?

options.A: The member continues to hold both positions
options.B: The seat is deemed vacant on entering office
options.C: The member must take leave of absence

questions.explanation: Under Article 158, if such a member is appointed Governor, the seat is deemed vacant on entering office.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who administers the oath of office to the Governor?

options.B: Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in the State

questions.explanation: The Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in the State administers the oath under Article 159.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: In the absence of the Chief Justice, who administers the oath to the Governor?

options.A: The Governor of a neighbouring State
options.B: The senior-most available Judge of that High Court

questions.explanation: In the Chief Justice's absence, the senior-most available Judge of that High Court administers it, under Article 159.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article vests the executive power of the State in the Governor?
questions.explanation: Under Article 154, the executive power of the State is vested in the Governor.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 154, the executive power of the Governor is exercised in accordance with which of the following?
questions.explanation: The executive power of the State is vested in the Governor and is exercised directly or through subordinate officers in accordance with the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who appoints the Chief Minister of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Governor appoints the Chief Minister under Article 164.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Section B and C

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: On whose advice does the Governor appoint other ministers?
questions.explanation: The Governor appoints other ministers on the advice of the Chief Minister under Article 164.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Section B and C

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 163, the Governor is ordinarily aided and advised by whom?

options.A: Chief Justice of the High Court
options.B: Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister

questions.explanation: Under Article 163, the Governor is ordinarily aided and advised by the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The scope of gubernatorial discretion has been explained by which authority?
questions.explanation: The scope of gubernatorial discretion has been explained by the Supreme Court in several judgments.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article does the Governor summon and prorogue the State Legislature and may dissolve the Legislative Assembly?
questions.explanation: The Governor summons and prorogues the State Legislature and may dissolve the Legislative Assembly under Article 174.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which Articles does the Governor address the Legislature?
questions.explanation: The Governor addresses the Legislature under Articles 175 and 176.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article does the Governor give or withhold assent to Bills, return certain Bills for reconsideration, or reserve Bills for the President?
questions.explanation: Article 200 deals with the Governor's power to give or withhold assent, return Bills, or reserve Bills for the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article can the Governor promulgate ordinances when the Legislature is not in session?
questions.explanation: Article 213 authorises the Governor to promulgate an ordinance when the Legislature is not in session.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: An ordinance promulgated by the Governor ordinarily ceases how long after reassembly unless approved?
questions.explanation: An ordinance must be laid before the Legislature and ordinarily ceases six weeks after reassembly unless approved or otherwise ceases earlier.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article does the Governor cause the annual financial statement (State Budget) to be laid before the Legislature?
questions.explanation: The Governor causes the annual financial statement to be laid before the Legislature under Article 202.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article does the Governor recommend demands for grants?
questions.explanation: The Governor recommends demands for grants under Article 203.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article can a Money Bill not be introduced in the Legislative Assembly without the Governor's recommendation?
questions.explanation: A Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Legislative Assembly without the Governor's recommendation under Article 207.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article does the Governor have pardoning powers?
questions.explanation: Article 161 empowers the Governor to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Governor's power to pardon a death sentence?

options.A: The Governor has the same power as the President under Article 72
options.B: The Governor does not possess the power to pardon a death sentence in the same manner as the President, but may suspend, remit or commute it
options.C: The Governor cannot interfere with a death sentence at all
options.D: The Governor can pardon a death sentence only with the Chief Justice's consent

questions.explanation: The Governor does not possess the power to pardon a death sentence in the same manner as the President under Article 72, but may suspend, remit or commute a death sentence under the constitutional and statutory framework.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 200, which of the following is NOT a power of the Governor regarding a Bill?

options.C: Return a non-Money Bill for reconsideration

questions.explanation: Article 200 permits the Governor to assent, withhold assent, return a non-Money Bill for reconsideration, or reserve a Bill for the President. The Governor cannot amend the Bill directly.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Reservation of a Bill for the President is mandatory in which situation?

options.A: When the Bill is a Money Bill
options.B: When the Bill would derogate from the powers of the High Court so as to endanger its constitutional position
options.C: When the Bill relates to agriculture
options.D: When the Bill is passed by a simple majority

questions.explanation: Reservation is mandatory in the constitutionally specified situation where the Bill would derogate from the powers of the High Court so as to endanger its constitutional position.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article may the President issue a proclamation of President's Rule if satisfied that the government of a State cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Under Article 356, the President may issue a proclamation if satisfied that the government of a State cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Governor's report in the context of President's Rule?

options.A: The Governor's report is constitutionally indispensable
options.B: The Governor's report may be a basis for the President's satisfaction, but a report is not constitutionally indispensable
options.C: The Governor cannot send any report to the President
options.D: The Governor's report is binding on the President

questions.explanation: The Governor's report may be a basis for the President's satisfaction, but a report is not constitutionally indispensable.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: A proclamation of President's Rule is subject to which of the following?
questions.explanation: The proclamation is subject to parliamentary approval and judicial review.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: Under which Article does the Governor appoint the Chief Minister?
questions.explanation: The Governor appoints the Chief Minister under Article 164.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: In ordinary circumstances, the Governor appoints which person as Chief Minister?

options.A: The person nominated by the President
options.B: The person who commands the confidence of the majority in the Legislative Assembly

questions.explanation: In ordinary circumstances, the Governor appoints the person who commands the confidence of the majority in the Legislative Assembly.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: To whom is the Council of Ministers collectively responsible?
questions.explanation: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly under Article 164(2).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: Under Article 164(1A), what is the maximum size of the Karnataka Council of Ministers including the Chief Minister?

options.A: 10 per cent of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly
options.B: 15 per cent of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly
options.C: 20 per cent of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly
options.D: 25 per cent of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly

questions.explanation: Under Article 164(1A), the total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, cannot exceed 15 per cent of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: What is the minimum number of ministers in the Karnataka Council of Ministers under Article 164(1A)?
questions.explanation: The number cannot be less than 12 under Article 164(1A).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: With 224 elected Assembly seats in Karnataka, what is the 15 per cent ceiling on the number of ministers?
questions.explanation: With 224 elected Assembly seats, the 15 per cent ceiling is 33 ministers (15% of 224 = 33.6, rounded to 33).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: The Chief Minister and other ministers hold office during whose pleasure?
questions.explanation: They hold office during the pleasure of the Governor, but in the parliamentary system this operates in accordance with constitutional conventions and the requirement that the ministry retain the confidence of the Legislative Assembly.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: What does collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers mean?

options.A: Each minister is individually answerable only to the Governor
options.B: The Council of Ministers stands or falls together and is answerable to the Legislative Assembly as a body
options.C: The Chief Minister alone is responsible
options.D: The Council is responsible to the Legislative Council

questions.explanation: Collective responsibility means the Council of Ministers stands or falls together and is answerable to the Legislative Assembly as a body.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: What does individual responsibility of a minister mean?

options.A: A minister holds office during the Governor's pleasure, normally exercised on the Chief Minister's advice
options.B: A minister is responsible only to the Legislative Council
options.C: A minister cannot be removed individually
options.D: A minister is responsible to the President

questions.explanation: Individual responsibility means a minister holds office during the Governor's pleasure, normally exercised on the Chief Minister's advice.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: Under Article 164(4), what happens to a minister who is not a member of either House of the State Legislature for six consecutive months?

options.B: The minister ceases to be a minister at the end of that period
options.C: The minister's term is extended by six months
options.D: The minister becomes a member automatically

questions.explanation: A minister who is not a member of either House of the State Legislature for six consecutive months ceases to be a minister at the end of that period, under Article 164(4).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: Who heads the State Government in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Chief Minister heads the State Government and leads the Council of Ministers.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: Which Article requires the Chief Minister to communicate to the Governor all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to State administration and legislative proposals?
questions.explanation: Article 167 requires the Chief Minister to communicate to the Governor all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to State administration and legislative proposals.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: Under Article 167, if the Governor so requires, the Chief Minister must submit for consideration of the Council any matter decided by whom?

options.B: An individual minister but not considered by the Council

questions.explanation: If the Governor so requires, the Chief Minister must submit for consideration of the Council any matter decided by an individual minister but not considered by the Council.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: What is the Cabinet?

options.B: The smaller, senior decision-making body within the Council of Ministers
options.C: A committee of the Legislative Assembly
options.D: A body of the Legislative Council

questions.explanation: The Cabinet is the smaller, senior decision-making body within the Council of Ministers.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: Which Amendment inserted Article 352(3), specifically referring to the Union Cabinet for recommending a National Emergency?
questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment inserted Article 352(3), which specifically refers to the Union Cabinet for the purpose of recommending a National Emergency.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 168, the Legislature of Karnataka consists of which of the following?

options.B: Governor, Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council

questions.explanation: Under Article 168, the Karnataka Legislature consists of the Governor, the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Where is the principal legislative complex of Karnataka located?
questions.explanation: The principal legislative complex is Vidhana Soudha in Bengaluru.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which building is also used for legislative sessions, particularly the designated northern Karnataka session?
questions.explanation: Suvarna Vidhana Soudha at Belagavi is also used for legislative sessions, particularly the designated northern Karnataka session.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the difference between the State Legislature and the State Government?

options.B: The Legislature is the law-making institution; the Government is the executive headed by the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
options.C: The Legislature is headed by the Chief Minister; the Government by the Governor
options.D: The Government makes laws; the Legislature implements them

questions.explanation: The State Legislature is the law-making institution consisting of the Governor and one or two Houses. The State Government is the executive headed by the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers. The ministry is politically accountable to the Legislative Assembly.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 169, a resolution for creation or abolition of a Legislative Council must be passed by the Legislative Assembly by which majority?

options.B: A majority of its total membership and a majority of not less than two-thirds of members present and voting

questions.explanation: Under Article 169, the Legislative Assembly must pass a resolution by a majority of its total membership and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of members present and voting.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: A law passed by Parliament to create or abolish a Legislative Council under Article 169 is treated as which of the following?

options.B: Not a constitutional amendment under Article 368

questions.explanation: Such a law is not treated as a constitutional amendment under Article 368.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 172, what is the normal duration of the Legislative Assembly?

options.B: Five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless sooner dissolved

questions.explanation: Under Article 172, the Legislative Assembly ordinarily continues for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless sooner dissolved.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: During a National Emergency, by how much can Parliament extend the term of the Legislative Assembly at a time?

options.B: One year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ceases

questions.explanation: During a National Emergency, Parliament may extend its term by law for one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ceases.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which House of the Karnataka Legislature is a continuing House and is not subject to dissolution?
questions.explanation: The Legislative Council is a continuing House and is not subject to dissolution.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Section D and F

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 174, what is the maximum interval between two sessions of the State Legislature?
questions.explanation: Under Article 174, six months must not intervene between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next session.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who presides over the Legislative Assembly of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Speaker presides over the Legislative Assembly.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who presides over the Legislative Council of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Chairman presides over the Legislative Council.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Section D and F

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who performs the Speaker's duties when the Speaker's office is vacant or the Speaker is absent?
questions.explanation: The Deputy Speaker performs the Speaker's duties when the Speaker's office is vacant or the Speaker is absent.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who performs the Chairman's duties when the Chairman's office is vacant or the Chairman is absent?
questions.explanation: The Deputy Chairman performs the corresponding duties when the Chairman's office is vacant or the Chairman is absent.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a main function of the Karnataka Legislature?

options.A: Making laws on matters within the State's legislative competence

questions.explanation: The Legislature makes laws on matters within the State's legislative competence; passes the State Budget; holds the executive accountable; debates public issues; and participates in specified constitutional functions such as electing the President through the electoral college.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How many elected seats are there in the Karnataka Legislative Assembly?
questions.explanation: The Assembly has 224 elected seats.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 170, what is the general constitutional range for the strength of a State Legislative Assembly?
questions.explanation: Article 170 sets the general constitutional range of 60 to 500 members, subject to constitutional exceptions and provisions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the normal term of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly?

options.B: Five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless sooner dissolved

questions.explanation: Five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless sooner dissolved, under Article 172.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How are members of the Legislative Assembly elected?

options.B: Directly by the people from territorial constituencies on the basis of adult suffrage

questions.explanation: Members are directly elected by the people from territorial constituencies on the basis of adult suffrage, subject to constitutional and statutory qualifications.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the minimum age to become a member of the Legislative Assembly?
questions.explanation: A person must be at least 25 years old to be chosen as a member of a State Legislative Assembly, under Article 173.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article does the Legislative Assembly choose its Speaker and Deputy Speaker?
questions.explanation: The Legislative Assembly chooses two of its members to be Speaker and Deputy Speaker under Article 178.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly decides disqualification petitions under which Schedule?
questions.explanation: The Speaker also decides disqualification petitions under the Tenth Schedule, subject to judicial review.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 179, the Speaker may be removed by a resolution of the Assembly passed by which majority?

options.A: Simple majority of members present and voting
options.B: A majority of all the then members of the Assembly
options.C: Two-thirds of members present and voting

questions.explanation: Under Article 179, the Speaker may be removed by a resolution of the Assembly passed by a majority of all the then members of the Assembly.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the minimum notice required for a resolution to remove the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly?
questions.explanation: At least 14 days' notice is required for such a resolution under Article 179.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 199, a Bill is a Money Bill in a State Legislature if it contains only provisions dealing with which matters?

options.B: Specified financial matters such as taxation, State borrowing, custody and withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of the State, appropriation and related matters

questions.explanation: Under Article 199, a Bill is a Money Bill if it contains only provisions dealing with specified financial matters such as taxation, State borrowing, custody and withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of the State, appropriation and related matters.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Whose decision on whether a Bill is a Money Bill is final under Article 199?
questions.explanation: The Speaker's decision on whether a Bill is a Money Bill is final under the Article, subject to constitutional interpretation by courts.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Can the Legislative Council amend or reject a State Money Bill?

options.A: Yes, it can amend and reject
options.B: No, it may only make recommendations and must return the Bill within 14 days
options.C: Yes, but only with the Governor's consent
options.D: It can reject but not amend

questions.explanation: The Council may make recommendations and must return the Money Bill to the Assembly within 14 days. The Assembly may accept or reject any or all recommendations.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: If the Legislative Council does not return a Money Bill within 14 days, what happens?

options.B: It is deemed passed by both Houses in the form passed by the Assembly

questions.explanation: If the Council does not return it within 14 days, it is deemed passed by both Houses in the form passed by the Assembly.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: For an ordinary Bill, what is the maximum delay the Legislative Council can cause across the two rounds under Article 197?
questions.explanation: For an ordinary Bill, the Council can delay passage for a maximum of about four months across the two rounds under Article 197: three months on the first consideration and one month after the Assembly repasses the Bill.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Can the Legislative Council permanently block an ordinary Bill?

options.A: Yes, it can permanently block it
options.B: No, it cannot permanently block an ordinary Bill; there is no provision for a joint sitting of the two State Houses

questions.explanation: The Council cannot permanently block an ordinary Bill; there is no provision for a joint sitting of the two State Houses.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is a no-confidence motion in the Karnataka Legislative Assembly?

options.A: A motion to remove the Governor
options.B: A motion that tests whether the Council of Ministers retains the confidence of the Assembly
options.C: A motion to dissolve the Legislative Council
options.D: A motion to amend the Constitution

questions.explanation: It is a motion that tests whether the Council of Ministers retains the confidence of the Assembly. Since the ministry is collectively responsible to the Assembly, defeat on a no-confidence motion ordinarily requires the ministry to resign.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What happens if the Council of Ministers is defeated on a no-confidence motion?

options.B: The ministry ordinarily has to resign

questions.explanation: Since the ministry is collectively responsible to the Assembly, defeat on a no-confidence motion ordinarily requires the ministry to resign.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Schedule contains the anti-defection law applicable to Karnataka MLAs?
questions.explanation: The Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985 and modified by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003, provides grounds for disqualification on defection.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The anti-defection law in the Tenth Schedule was added by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The Tenth Schedule was added by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Tenth Schedule was modified by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The Tenth Schedule was modified by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who decides disqualification petitions under the Tenth Schedule, subject to judicial review?

options.D: The Chief Justice of the High Court

questions.explanation: The Presiding Officer decides such petitions, subject to judicial review.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How many members are there in the Karnataka Legislative Council?
questions.explanation: The Council has a sanctioned strength of 75 members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 171, a State Legislative Council cannot exceed what fraction of the strength of the Legislative Assembly?
questions.explanation: Article 171 provides that a State Legislative Council cannot exceed one-third of the strength of the Legislative Assembly.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the minimum number of members a State Legislative Council can have under Article 171?
questions.explanation: Article 171 provides that a State Legislative Council cannot have fewer than 40 members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: As nearly as possible, how often do one-third of the members of the Legislative Council retire?
questions.explanation: As nearly as possible, one-third of its members retire every second year under Article 172(2).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the minimum age to become a member of the Legislative Council?
questions.explanation: A person must be at least 30 years old to be chosen as a member of a State Legislative Council, under Article 173.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 171, what fraction of Legislative Council members is elected by local authorities?
questions.explanation: Under Article 171, as nearly as may be, one-third are elected by local authorities.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 171, what fraction of Legislative Council members is elected by graduates?
questions.explanation: Under Article 171, as nearly as may be, one-twelfth are elected by graduates.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 171, what fraction of Legislative Council members is elected by teachers?
questions.explanation: Under Article 171, as nearly as may be, one-twelfth are elected by teachers.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 171, what fraction of Legislative Council members is elected by members of the Legislative Assembly?
questions.explanation: Under Article 171, as nearly as may be, one-third are elected by members of the Legislative Assembly from among persons who are not Assembly members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who nominates the remaining members of the Legislative Council after elections?
questions.explanation: The remainder are nominated by the Governor under Article 171.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 171(5), the Governor nominates persons having special knowledge or practical experience in which fields?

options.A: Literature, science, art, cooperative movement or social service
options.B: Law, medicine, engineering, agriculture or trade
options.C: Defence, foreign affairs, finance, commerce or industry
options.D: Sports, cinema, music, dance or drama

questions.explanation: The Governor nominates persons having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, cooperative movement or social service, under Article 171(5).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the role of the Legislative Council?

options.B: It reviews and debates legislation, suggests amendments, represents special electorates, and provides a revising chamber
options.C: It controls the Council of Ministers

questions.explanation: It reviews and debates legislation, suggests amendments, represents local authorities, graduates and teachers through special electorates, and provides a revising chamber. Its powers are weaker than those of the Legislative Assembly, especially in financial matters and government formation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Can the Legislative Council remove the Chief Minister or Council of Ministers?

options.B: No, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly, not the Legislative Council

questions.explanation: No. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly, not to the Legislative Council. The Council cannot pass a binding no-confidence motion that removes the ministry.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article does the Legislative Council elect a Chairman and Deputy Chairman from among its members?
questions.explanation: The Chairman presides over the Council under Article 182. The Council elects a Chairman and Deputy Chairman from among its members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides that there shall be a High Court for each State?
questions.explanation: Article 214 provides that there shall be a High Court for each State, subject to constitutional provisions permitting a common High Court for two or more States or Union Territories.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Where is the principal seat of the High Court of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The principal seat is at Bengaluru.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Where are the permanent benches of the High Court of Karnataka located?
questions.explanation: The High Court also has permanent benches at Dharwad and Kalaburgi.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: When did the High Court of the reorganised Mysore State come into being?
questions.explanation: Following the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, the High Court of the reorganised Mysore State came into being on 1 November 1956.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: When was the State renamed Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The State was renamed Karnataka on 1 November 1973, and the High Court came to be known as the High Court of Karnataka.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The High Court's principal seat in Bengaluru functions in which historic building?
questions.explanation: The High Court's principal seat in Bengaluru functions in the historic Attara Kacheri building opposite Vidhana Soudha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Attara Kacheri building originally housed offices of which administration?
questions.explanation: The building originally housed offices of the erstwhile Mysore administration and became the seat of the High Court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 216, every High Court consists of which of the following?

options.A: A Chief Justice and such other Judges as the President may from time to time deem necessary to appoint
options.B: A Chief Justice and a fixed number of 30 Judges
options.D: A Chief Justice and Judges appointed by the Governor

questions.explanation: Under Article 216, every High Court consists of a Chief Justice and such other Judges as the President may from time to time deem necessary to appoint.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who appoints the Chief Justice and other Judges of the Karnataka High Court?
questions.explanation: The President appoints High Court Judges under Article 217 after the constitutionally required consultation process.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 217, the appointment of a High Court Judge requires consultation with which authorities?

options.A: The Chief Justice of India, the Governor of the State and, for appointment of a Judge other than the Chief Justice, the Chief Justice of the High Court
options.B: Only the Chief Justice of India
options.D: The President, the Prime Minister and the Chief Minister

questions.explanation: The President appoints High Court Judges under Article 217 after the constitutionally required consultation process, including consultation with the Chief Justice of India, the Governor of the State and, for appointment of a Judge other than the Chief Justice, the Chief Justice of the High Court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 217, a Judge of a High Court holds office until attaining what age?
questions.explanation: A Judge of a High Court holds office until attaining 62 years of age, under Article 217.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 217, what qualifications are required to be appointed a High Court Judge?

options.A: Citizen of India and must have held a judicial office in India for at least ten years, or have been an advocate of a High Court for at least ten years
options.B: Citizen of India and must have completed 35 years of age
options.C: Must be a member of the Bar for at least five years
options.D: Must be a District Judge for at least three years

questions.explanation: The person must be a citizen of India and must have held a judicial office in India for at least ten years, or have been an advocate of a High Court (or two or more such Courts in succession) for at least ten years, under Article 217.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: A High Court Judge may be removed by the President on which grounds?

options.B: Loss of confidence of the Governor

questions.explanation: A High Court Judge may be removed by the President in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court: proved misbehaviour or incapacity, following the prescribed parliamentary address and special-majority process.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article may the High Court issue directions, orders or writs including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari?
questions.explanation: Under Article 226, the High Court may issue directions, orders or writs, including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari, for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The writ jurisdiction of the High Court under Article 226 is wider in subject matter than which jurisdiction of the Supreme Court?
questions.explanation: This jurisdiction is wider in subject matter than Article 32 jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article does the High Court have superintendence over all courts and tribunals throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction?
questions.explanation: Article 227 gives the High Court superintendence over all courts and tribunals throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction, subject to constitutional exceptions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Judicial review by the High Court is part of which feature of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Judicial review is part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article is control over district courts and courts subordinate thereto vested in the High Court?
questions.explanation: Under Article 235, control over district courts and courts subordinate thereto, including posting, promotion and leave of persons belonging to the State judicial service, is vested in the High Court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 235, the High Court's control over subordinate courts includes which of the following?

options.A: Posting, promotion and leave of persons belonging to the State judicial service

questions.explanation: Under Article 235, control over district courts and courts subordinate thereto, including posting, promotion and leave of persons belonging to the State judicial service, is vested in the High Court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the State Secretariat?

options.A: The central administrative machinery of the State Government

questions.explanation: The State Secretariat is the central administrative machinery of the State Government. It assists the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers in policy formulation, coordination, inter-departmental consultation, Cabinet work, legislative business and monitoring implementation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who is the senior-most civil servant in the State and the principal administrative adviser to the State Government?
questions.explanation: The Chief Secretary is the senior-most civil servant in the State and the principal administrative adviser to the State Government.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The post of Chief Secretary is which type of office?

options.A: A constitutional office created by a specific Article
options.B: An administrative office, not a constitutional office created by a specific Article

questions.explanation: The post is an administrative office, not a constitutional office created by a specific Article.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who is the principal district-level representative of the State administration in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Deputy Commissioner is the principal district-level representative of the State administration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following functions does the Deputy Commissioner commonly perform?

options.A: Revenue, land administration, election-related, disaster-management and coordination functions

questions.explanation: The Deputy Commissioner commonly performs revenue, land administration, election-related, disaster-management and coordination functions under applicable laws and government rules.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: In many districts, the Deputy Commissioner also functions as which authority for specified executive-magisterial purposes?
questions.explanation: In many districts the Deputy Commissioner also functions as District Magistrate for specified executive-magisterial purposes.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who heads district police administration and maintains public order within the district?
questions.explanation: The Superintendent of Police heads district police administration, maintains public order and supervises crime prevention and investigation within the district.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Superintendent of Police functions subject to which framework?

options.A: The Police Act, criminal procedure law and State rules

questions.explanation: The Superintendent of Police heads district police administration, maintains public order and supervises crime prevention and investigation within the district, subject to the Police Act, criminal procedure law and State rules.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the difference between the Deputy Commissioner and the Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officer?

options.A: The Deputy Commissioner heads the district's general/revenue administration; the CEO heads the executive administration of the rural local-government institution under the Karnataka Panchayat Raj framework
options.C: The CEO heads revenue administration; the Deputy Commissioner heads the Panchayat
options.D: The Deputy Commissioner is a judicial officer; the CEO is a police officer

questions.explanation: The Deputy Commissioner heads the district's general/revenue administration and performs functions assigned under law. The Chief Executive Officer of the Zilla Panchayat heads the executive administration of the rural local-government institution under the Karnataka Panchayat Raj framework. Their roles are distinct, although coordination is required.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the Karnataka Administrative Service (KAS)?

options.A: A State civil service through which officers perform executive, revenue, developmental and administrative functions

questions.explanation: KAS is a State civil service through which officers perform executive, revenue, developmental and administrative functions in State departments and field offices.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which body performs recruitment functions for the Karnataka Administrative Service (KAS)?
questions.explanation: Recruitment and service matters are governed by State rules, with the Karnataka Public Service Commission performing recruitment functions assigned to it.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: When was the reorganised Mysore State formed after linguistic reorganisation?
questions.explanation: The reorganised Mysore State was formed on 1 November 1956 under the States Reorganisation framework.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: When was Mysore State renamed Karnataka?
questions.explanation: It was renamed Karnataka on 1 November 1973.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: When was the first Assembly of Mysore State under the Constitution constituted?
questions.explanation: The first Assembly under the Constitution was constituted in 1952.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: When did the reorganised State's first Assembly sitting in the newly built Vidhana Soudha take place?
questions.explanation: The reorganised State's first Assembly sitting in the newly built Vidhana Soudha took place on 19 December 1956.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: When was Vidhana Soudha inaugurated?
questions.explanation: Vidhana Soudha was inaugurated in 1956 and became the principal seat of the Karnataka Legislature and State Secretariat.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Vidhana Soudha was built under the leadership of which Chief Minister?
questions.explanation: It was built under the leadership of Chief Minister Kengal Hanumanthaiah.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the two Houses of the Karnataka Legislature and their strengths?

options.A: Legislative Assembly: 224 elected seats; Legislative Council: 75 members
options.B: Legislative Assembly: 250 seats; Legislative Council: 100 members
options.C: Legislative Assembly: 200 seats; Legislative Council: 60 members
options.D: Legislative Assembly: 224 seats; Legislative Council: 40 members

questions.explanation: The Legislative Assembly has 224 elected seats. The Legislative Council has a sanctioned strength of 75 members.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which House of the Karnataka Legislature is permanent?
questions.explanation: The Legislative Council is permanent; the Legislative Assembly ordinarily has a five-year term and may be dissolved earlier.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which House of the Karnataka Legislature controls the Council of Ministers?
questions.explanation: The Legislative Assembly, because the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to it under Article 164(2).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Karnataka institution is the highest court in the State?
questions.explanation: The High Court of Karnataka, with its principal seat at Bengaluru and permanent benches at Dharwad and Kalaburgi, is the highest court in the State.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which official body provides legislative records, bills, proceedings and committee information for Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Karnataka Legislature's official website provides Assembly and Council information, including bills, debates, questions, committees, bulletins and legislative records.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Articles 153 to 162 of the Constitution deal with which topic?
questions.explanation: As per the Quick Article Revision table, Articles 153-162 deal with the Governor.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Quick Article Revision

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Articles 163 to 167 of the Constitution deal with which topic?
questions.explanation: As per the Quick Article Revision table, Articles 163-167 deal with Council of Ministers / Chief Minister.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Quick Article Revision

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Articles 168 to 177 of the Constitution deal with which topic?
questions.explanation: As per the Quick Article Revision table, Articles 168-177 deal with the State Legislature.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Quick Article Revision

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Articles deal with the Legislative Assembly according to the Quick Article Revision table?
questions.explanation: As per the Quick Article Revision table, the Legislative Assembly is covered under Articles 170, 172, 178-195.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Quick Article Revision

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Articles deal with the Legislative Council according to the Quick Article Revision table?
questions.explanation: As per the Quick Article Revision table, the Legislative Council is covered under Articles 169, 171, 172, 182-193.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Quick Article Revision

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Articles 196 to 201 of the Constitution deal with which topic?
questions.explanation: As per the Quick Article Revision table, Articles 196-201 deal with Bills / Money Bills / Assent.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Quick Article Revision

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Articles 202 to 207 of the Constitution deal with which topic?
questions.explanation: As per the Quick Article Revision table, Articles 202-207 deal with Budget and financial procedure.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Quick Article Revision

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Articles 208 to 212 of the Constitution deal with which topic?
questions.explanation: As per the Quick Article Revision table, Articles 208-212 deal with Legislative procedure / privileges.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Quick Article Revision

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Articles 214 to 231 of the Constitution deal with which topic?
questions.explanation: As per the Quick Article Revision table, Articles 214-231 deal with High Courts.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Quick Article Revision

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Articles 233 to 237 of the Constitution deal with which topic?
questions.explanation: As per the Quick Article Revision table, Articles 233-237 deal with Subordinate courts.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Quick Article Revision

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Governor's ordinance-making power under Article 213 can be exercised when which condition is met?

options.A: When the Legislative Assembly is not in session, or where the State has two Houses, when both Houses are not in session, and immediate action is necessary
options.B: Only when the Legislative Assembly is dissolved
options.D: Only with the President's prior approval

questions.explanation: Article 213 authorises the Governor to promulgate an ordinance when the Legislative Assembly is not in session, or where the State has two Houses, when both Houses are not in session, and immediate action is necessary.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: An ordinance promulgated by the Governor has what force?

options.A: It has the force of law
options.C: It has no legal force until ratified by Parliament
options.D: It has the force of a constitutional amendment

questions.explanation: An ordinance has the force of law but must be laid before the Legislature and ordinarily ceases six weeks after reassembly unless approved or otherwise ceases earlier.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Governor's pardoning power under Article 161 extends to cases relating to which matters?

options.A: Matters within the State's executive power

questions.explanation: Article 161 empowers the Governor to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment, or to suspend, remit or commute sentences, in cases relating to matters within the State's executive power.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Governor's discretion under Article 163?

options.B: Discretion is limited to matters in which the Constitution expressly or necessarily provides for it
options.C: The Governor has no discretion at all
options.D: Discretion is exercised only on the Chief Minister's advice

questions.explanation: Under Article 163, the Governor is ordinarily aided and advised by the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister. Discretion is limited to matters in which the Constitution expressly or necessarily provides for it.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: Which of the following is a main function of the Chief Minister?

options.A: Administering the oath to the Governor
options.B: Acting as the principal link between the Governor and the Council of Ministers

questions.explanation: The Chief Minister heads the State Government, leads the Council of Ministers, allocates or coordinates ministerial portfolios, advises the Governor on ministerial appointments and legislative matters, communicates Cabinet decisions to the Governor, and acts as the principal link between the Governor and the Council of Ministers.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Karnataka Legislature?

options.A: Making laws on matters within the State's legislative competence
options.B: Passing the State Budget and authorising public expenditure
options.C: Holding the executive accountable through questions, motions and committees
options.D: Appointing the Chief Justice of the High Court

questions.explanation: The Legislature makes laws, passes the Budget, holds the executive accountable, debates public issues, and participates in specified constitutional functions such as electing the President through the electoral college. It does not appoint the Chief Justice of the High Court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 197, how long can the Legislative Council delay an ordinary Bill on first consideration?
questions.explanation: For an ordinary Bill, the Council can delay passage for a maximum of about four months across the two rounds under Article 197: three months on the first consideration and one month after the Assembly repasses the Bill.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 197, after the Assembly repasses an ordinary Bill, how long can the Legislative Council delay it?
questions.explanation: Under Article 197, the Council can delay for three months on the first consideration and one month after the Assembly repasses the Bill.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which special electorates are represented in the Karnataka Legislative Council?
questions.explanation: The Council represents local authorities, graduates and teachers through special electorates and provides a revising chamber.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The High Court of Karnataka exercises jurisdiction over which territory?

options.C: Only the districts of Dharwad and Kalaburgi
options.D: Only the districts of Mysuru and Mangaluru

questions.explanation: Following the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, the High Court of the reorganised Mysore State came into being on 1 November 1956, exercising jurisdiction over the reorganised State, which was renamed Karnataka on 1 November 1973.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following writs can the High Court issue under Article 226?

options.A: Habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari

questions.explanation: Under Article 226, the High Court may issue directions, orders or writs, including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the State Secretariat?

options.A: Assisting the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers in policy formulation and coordination

questions.explanation: The State Secretariat assists the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers in policy formulation, coordination, inter-departmental consultation, Cabinet work, legislative business and monitoring implementation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the Chief Secretary of Karnataka?

options.A: Coordinating departments and supporting Cabinet and inter-departmental administration
options.B: Administering the oath to the Governor

questions.explanation: The Chief Secretary coordinates departments, supports Cabinet and inter-departmental administration, and oversees important administrative matters.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officer heads the executive administration of which institution?

options.A: The rural local-government institution under the Karnataka Panchayat Raj framework

questions.explanation: The Chief Executive Officer of the Zilla Panchayat heads the executive administration of the rural local-government institution under the Karnataka Panchayat Raj framework.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The High Court of Karnataka heads which system in the State?
questions.explanation: The High Court of Karnataka heads the State judicial system.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a constitutional Part/Article with its subject?

options.D: Part III, Articles 12-35 — State Election Commission

questions.explanation: State Executive is covered under Part VI, Articles 153-167.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Governor is entitled to which of the following under Article 158?

options.A: The official residence, emoluments and allowances prescribed by law
options.B: A seat in the Legislative Assembly
options.C: A vote in the Legislative Council

questions.explanation: Article 158 provides that the Governor is entitled to the official residence, emoluments and allowances prescribed by law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 158, the Governor cannot hold which of the following?
questions.explanation: Article 158 provides that the Governor cannot hold another office of profit.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: If a Governor's term expires but a successor has not entered office, what happens?

options.A: The Governor may continue until a successor enters office
options.B: The office becomes vacant and the Chief Justice takes over
options.C: The President must immediately appoint an acting Governor
options.D: The Legislative Assembly elects a new Governor

questions.explanation: Under Article 156, the normal term is five years, but the Governor may continue until a successor enters office and may be removed earlier by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a financial power of the Governor?

options.A: Causing the annual financial statement to be laid before the Legislature
options.C: Recommending the introduction of a Money Bill
options.D: Passing the Finance Bill directly without the Legislature

questions.explanation: The Governor causes the annual financial statement to be laid under Article 202, recommends demands for grants under Article 203, and recommends Money Bills under Article 207. The Governor does not pass the Finance Bill directly.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: A ministry that loses the confidence of the Legislative Assembly must do which of the following?

options.A: Continue in office until the next election
options.B: Resign or face the constitutional consequences

questions.explanation: A ministry that loses the confidence of the House must resign or face the constitutional consequences.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Chief Minister?

options.B: Advising the Governor on ministerial appointments
options.C: Communicating Cabinet decisions to the Governor
options.D: Administering the oath to the Governor

questions.explanation: The Chief Minister heads the State Government, leads the Council of Ministers, allocates or coordinates ministerial portfolios, advises the Governor on ministerial appointments and legislative matters, communicates Cabinet decisions to the Governor, and acts as the principal link between the Governor and the Council of Ministers. The oath to the Governor is administered by the Chief Justice of the High Court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The State Legislature is politically accountable through which mechanism?

options.A: The ministry is politically accountable to the Legislative Assembly
options.B: The ministry is politically accountable to the Legislative Council
options.C: The ministry is politically accountable to the Governor
options.D: The ministry is politically accountable to the President

questions.explanation: The ministry is politically accountable to the Legislative Assembly.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a principal power of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly?

options.A: Presiding over Assembly sittings and maintaining order
options.B: Administering the oath to the Governor

questions.explanation: The Speaker presides over Assembly sittings, maintains order, interprets and applies the Rules of Procedure, decides points of order, oversees legislative business and performs functions assigned by the Constitution and rules.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 179, the Speaker may vacate office in which of the following ways?

options.A: By ceasing to be a member, by resigning to the Deputy Speaker, or by removal through a resolution of the Assembly
options.B: Only by completing a five-year term
options.D: Only by a Supreme Court order

questions.explanation: Under Article 179, the Speaker may vacate office if ceasing to be a member, may resign to the Deputy Speaker, or may be removed by a resolution of the Assembly passed by a majority of all the then members of the Assembly.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: If the Legislative Council returns a Money Bill with recommendations, what can the Assembly do?

options.A: The Assembly may accept or reject any or all recommendations
options.B: The Assembly must accept all recommendations
options.C: The Assembly must send the Bill to the Governor
options.D: The Assembly must convene a joint sitting

questions.explanation: The Assembly may accept or reject any or all recommendations.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Legislative Council's powers are weaker than those of the Legislative Assembly especially in which matters?
questions.explanation: Its powers are weaker than those of the Legislative Assembly, especially in financial matters and government formation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The High Court may review the constitutionality and legality of which actions within its jurisdiction?
questions.explanation: The High Court may review the constitutionality and legality of legislative and executive action within its jurisdiction.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The High Court's superintendence under Article 227 extends over which bodies?

options.A: All courts and tribunals throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction

questions.explanation: Article 227 gives the High Court superintendence over all courts and tribunals throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction, subject to constitutional exceptions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Deputy Commissioner and the Zilla Panchayat CEO are required to do which of the following?

options.A: Coordinate with each other although their roles are distinct

questions.explanation: Their roles are distinct, although coordination is required.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following constitutional Parts and Articles are especially relevant to the Karnataka Government?

options.A: Part VI, Articles 153-167 (State Executive); Part VI, Articles 168-212 (State Legislature); Part VI, Articles 214-231 (High Courts)
options.B: Part III, Articles 12-35 (State Executive); Part IV, Articles 36-51 (State Legislature)
options.C: Part V, Articles 52-151 (High Courts); Part VII (State Legislature)

questions.explanation: State Executive: Part VI, Articles 153-167; State Legislature: Part VI, Articles 168-212; High Courts: Part VI, Articles 214-231.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Governor appoints which of the following officials?

options.B: The Chief Justice of the High Court
options.C: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly

questions.explanation: The Governor appoints the Advocate General and performs other constitutional appointments and functions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 169, after the Legislative Assembly passes the resolution, who may pass a law to create or abolish the Council?
questions.explanation: Under Article 169, the Legislative Assembly must pass a resolution, and Parliament may then pass a law to create or abolish the Council.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a category of membership in the Karnataka Legislative Council?
questions.explanation: Under Article 171, members are elected by local authorities, graduates, teachers, and members of the Legislative Assembly, and some are nominated by the Governor. There is no direct election by the people for the Council.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The High Court of Karnataka came to be known by its present name in which year?
questions.explanation: The State was renamed Karnataka on 1 November 1973, and the High Court came to be known as the High Court of Karnataka.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: KAS officers perform their functions in which of the following?
questions.explanation: KAS is a State civil service through which officers perform executive, revenue, developmental and administrative functions in State departments and field offices.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 200, the Governor may return which type of Bill for reconsideration?
questions.explanation: Article 200 permits the Governor to assent to a Bill, withhold assent, return a non-Money Bill for reconsideration, or reserve a Bill for the consideration of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: A Money Bill in the State Legislature is defined under which Article?
questions.explanation: Under Article 199, a Bill is a Money Bill if it contains only provisions dealing with specified financial matters.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Speaker's decision on whether a Bill is a Money Bill is final under Article 199, subject to which of the following?
questions.explanation: The Speaker's decision on whether a Bill is a Money Bill is final under the Article, subject to constitutional interpretation by courts.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Legislative Assembly chooses how many of its members to be Speaker and Deputy Speaker?

options.B: Two members — Speaker and Deputy Speaker

questions.explanation: The Legislative Assembly chooses two of its members to be Speaker and Deputy Speaker under Article 178.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Legislative Council elects its Chairman and Deputy Chairman from among whom?
questions.explanation: The Council elects a Chairman and Deputy Chairman from among its members under Article 182.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: A High Court Judge may be removed by the President in the same manner and on the same grounds as which other judge?

options.A: A Judge of the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: A High Court Judge may be removed by the President in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court: proved misbehaviour or incapacity, following the prescribed parliamentary address and special-majority process.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 217, a person must have been an advocate of a High Court for at least how many years to be appointed a High Court Judge?
questions.explanation: The person must have held a judicial office in India for at least ten years, or have been an advocate of a High Court for at least ten years, under Article 217.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 217, a person must have held a judicial office in India for at least how many years to be appointed a High Court Judge?
questions.explanation: The person must have held a judicial office in India for at least ten years, or have been an advocate of a High Court for at least ten years, under Article 217.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Superintendent of Police supervises which of the following within the district?
questions.explanation: The Superintendent of Police heads district police administration, maintains public order and supervises crime prevention and investigation within the district.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 159, the oath is administered to the Governor by the Chief Justice of which court?

options.A: The High Court exercising jurisdiction in the State

questions.explanation: The Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in the State administers the oath under Article 159.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Karnataka Legislature participates in which constitutional function mentioned in the notes?

options.A: Electing the President through the electoral college
options.B: Appointing the Chief Justice of India

questions.explanation: The Legislature participates in specified constitutional functions such as electing the President through the electoral college.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 173, what is the minimum age to become a member of the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council respectively?
questions.explanation: A person must be at least 25 years old for the Legislative Assembly and at least 30 years old for the Legislative Council, under Article 173.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Sections E and F

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Governor causes supplementary, additional or excess grants to be presented as required by which framework?
questions.explanation: The Governor causes supplementary, additional or excess grants to be presented as constitutionally required.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.topic: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: Which Article makes the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly?
questions.explanation: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly under Article 164(2).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Karnataka State executive?
questions.explanation: The State executive consists of the Governor, the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers, with the Advocate General as the State's highest law officer. The Speaker is a legislative office, not part of the executive.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The High Court's principal seat at Bengaluru is located opposite which building?
questions.explanation: The High Court's principal seat in Bengaluru functions in the historic Attara Kacheri building opposite Vidhana Soudha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 171, the members elected by the Legislative Assembly must be chosen from among which persons?

options.A: Persons who are not Assembly members

questions.explanation: Under Article 171, one-third are elected by members of the Legislative Assembly from among persons who are not Assembly members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 155, the Governor is appointed by warrant under whose hand and seal?
questions.explanation: The President of India appoints the Governor by warrant under his or her hand and seal under Article 155.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Legislative Assembly ordinarily continues for five years from which date?

options.A: The date appointed for its first meeting
options.B: The date of the election notification
options.C: The date of the Governor's assent
options.D: The date of the Budget presentation

questions.explanation: Under Article 172, the Legislative Assembly ordinarily continues for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless sooner dissolved.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Section D and E

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The State Secretariat assists the Council of Ministers in which of the following?

options.B: Administering the oath to the Governor

questions.explanation: The State Secretariat assists the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers in policy formulation, coordination, inter-departmental consultation, Cabinet work, legislative business and monitoring implementation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the High Court's writ jurisdiction compared to the Supreme Court's Article 32 jurisdiction?

options.A: The High Court's jurisdiction is wider in subject matter
options.B: The High Court's jurisdiction is narrower in subject matter
options.D: The High Court has no writ jurisdiction

questions.explanation: This jurisdiction is wider in subject matter than Article 32 jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The State Legislature holds the executive accountable through which of the following?
questions.explanation: It holds the executive accountable through questions, motions and committees.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: If the Legislative Council does not return a Money Bill within 14 days, the Bill is deemed passed by both Houses in which form?

options.A: In the form passed by the Assembly
options.B: In the form recommended by the Council
options.C: In the form amended by the Governor
options.D: In the form proposed by the Chief Minister

questions.explanation: If the Council does not return it within 14 days, it is deemed passed by both Houses in the form passed by the Assembly.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Legislative Council is a continuing House. What does this mean?

options.A: It is not subject to dissolution

questions.explanation: The Legislative Council is a continuing House and is not subject to dissolution.
questions.source: Karnataka Government Notes, Section D and F
